nodes.rationale: Replace hardcoded dimension constants with DesignProvider token calls so the whole UI scales proportionally with UIConfig; avoids magic numbers, enables accessibility scaling, and keeps rounding consistent via MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero.

nodes.label: UI Scaling Formula
nodes.rationale: valor_final = round(valor_base x multiplicador_densidad x factor_escala); guarantees proportional, consistent scaling of every UI dimension across scale and density settings, using MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero.

nodes.label: FSP Pattern adapted to Java
nodes.rationale: Swapping the UI implementation (console -> JavaFX) should require changing exactly one line in the Composition Root; a Panel/View never publishes External events, only the Service/Logic does.

nodes.label: Visitor / Double Dispatch pattern
nodes.rationale: Eliminates instanceof/switch-by-type which would violate OCP; each controller type presents itself via accept(visitor), and the view implements one visit() overload per concrete type, so adding a type only requires implementing the contract, not modifying the view.

nodes.label: GRASP: Information Expert
nodes.rationale: Assign the responsibility to the class that has the information necessary to fulfill it.

nodes.label: GRASP: High Cohesion
nodes.rationale: A class does closely related things; split it if it does too much or disparate things.

nodes.label: GRASP: Low Coupling
nodes.rationale: Minimize dependencies between classes; prefer depending on abstractions, not concretes.

nodes.label: GRASP: Controller
nodes.rationale: System events are received by a Controller class, never the UI; the UI delegates.

nodes.label: GRASP: Creator
nodes.rationale: B creates A if B contains, aggregates, records, or uses A, or has A's initialization data.

nodes.label: GRASP: Pure Fabrication
nodes.rationale: If assigning a responsibility violates cohesion or coupling, create an artificial class to encapsulate it.

nodes.label: GRASP: Indirection
nodes.rationale: To decouple two classes, introduce an intermediary between them.

nodes.label: GRASP: Polymorphism
nodes.rationale: When behavior varies by type, use polymorphic operations. Never instanceof or switch by type.

nodes.label: GRASP: Protected Variations
nodes.rationale: Identify points of variation or instability and build a stable interface around them.

nodes.label: SOLID: Single Responsibility Principle
nodes.rationale: A class has a single reason to change; if it changes for two distinct reasons, split it.

nodes.label: SOLID: Open/Closed Principle
nodes.rationale: Open to extension (new derived classes), closed to modification (do not touch working code).

nodes.label: SOLID: Liskov Substitution Principle
nodes.rationale: A subclass must be substitutable for its base class without breaking the program.

nodes.label: SOLID: Interface Segregation Principle
nodes.rationale: Clients should not depend on interfaces they do not use; prefer several cohesive interfaces to one fat one.

nodes.label: SOLID: Dependency Inversion Principle
nodes.rationale: High-level modules do not depend on low-level modules; both depend on abstractions.

nodes.label: YAGNI
nodes.rationale: Do not apply a principle speculatively when there is no real point of variation.

nodes.label: DRY Principle
nodes.rationale: Do not repeat logic; a single representation of each piece of knowledge.

nodes.label: KISS Principle
nodes.rationale: The simplest solution that works correctly; avoid unnecessary complexity.

nodes.label: State pattern
nodes.rationale: An object changes its behavior based on internal state; avoids if/switch by state.

nodes.label: Command pattern
nodes.rationale: Encapsulate an action as an object (undo, menu, operation queue).

nodes.label: Observer pattern
nodes.rationale: An object notifies others without knowing them; decoupled subject + subscribers.

nodes.label: Strategy pattern
nodes.rationale: The algorithm varies but the structure is fixed; inject the concrete strategy.

nodes.label: Template Method pattern
nodes.rationale: The algorithm skeleton is fixed; some steps vary in subclasses.

nodes.label: Iterator pattern
nodes.rationale: Traverse a collection without exposing its internal representation.

nodes.label: Chain of Responsibility pattern
nodes.rationale: A request passes through a chain of handlers until one processes it.

nodes.label: Singleton pattern
nodes.rationale: Only if it passes the mandatory gate in steering/05-pattern-gates.md - 'only one instance can exist' alone is not enough.

nodes.label: Factory Method pattern
nodes.rationale: The base class delegates object creation to subclasses.

nodes.label: Abstract Factory pattern
nodes.rationale: Families of related objects must be created without specifying their concrete classes.

nodes.label: Builder pattern
nodes.rationale: Constructing a complex object requires many steps or variants.

nodes.label: Prototype pattern
nodes.rationale: Cloning an existing instance is more efficient than building from scratch.

nodes.label: Adapter pattern
nodes.rationale: Make an incompatible interface compatible with another without modifying its code.

nodes.label: Composite pattern
nodes.rationale: Treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly (a tree).

nodes.label: Decorator pattern
nodes.rationale: Add responsibilities to an object dynamically without inheritance.

nodes.label: Facade pattern
nodes.rationale: Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.

nodes.label: Null Object pattern
nodes.rationale: Avoid null checks by substituting null with an object that has empty behavior.

nodes.label: Proxy pattern
nodes.rationale: Control access to an object (lazy loading, security, logging).

nodes.label: Singleton Gate (12-criteria GoF checklist)
nodes.rationale: Only 1 of 12 audited classes in the reference project passed the gate; default to constructor injection from the composition root instead of getInstance(), unless the class fits a valid infrastructure category and passes all thread-safety/SOLID/testability checks.

nodes.label: Singleton Alternatives (DI, Factory, Builder, Flyweight, Context Object...)
FSP Model (Feature/Service/Panel)
nodes.rationale: Panel only builds UI controls and exposes mutator methods; Service validates, persists and publishes External events; App is the sole composition root. Eliminates callback hell by having components publish Internal messages instead of passing Action<T> callbacks.

nodes.label: Layered DAG (Acyclic Dependencies Principle)
nodes.rationale: Layers form a strict DAG - events/libs <- models <- controllers <- views <- core; a lower layer importing from core is an architectural error; core is the only layer that knows concrete implementations of every other layer.

nodes.label: Explicit braces in all control flow
Dictionary instead of switch for dispatch/mapping
nodes.rationale: When every switch branch just dispatches an action or maps a key to a value with no complex per-branch state mutation, replace it with a Dictionary<TKey,Action|TValue>; switch remains valid only for genuine state-machine branches with different multi-statement logic per case.

nodes.label: assert for logical contracts; exceptions for external errors
nodes.rationale: assert expresses preconditions/postconditions/invariants indicating a programmer bug; never used for user input or external resource errors, which must use exceptions instead.

nodes.label: No instanceof/switch by type - use Visitor
nodes.rationale: instanceof and switch(obj.getClass()) are prohibited because they break OCP and the GRASP Polymorphism principle; use double-dispatch Visitor instead.

nodes.label: Blank line between every field and method
Design by Contract (pre/post/invariants)
nodes.rationale: Each non-trivial method should be statable as an explicit contract; preconditions via assert at method start, postconditions/invariants after the operation when the result is not obvious.
